SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY — TERMLY EXAM #2
====

GRADE: Grade 5
SUBJECT: SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Burning crop residue every week
   B. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   C. Removing all vegetation
   D. Overgrazing continuously

2. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Movement of water only across a membrane
   B. A chemical reaction forming ash
   C. Heating until a solid melts
   D. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

3. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water removes heat too quickly
   B. Petrol fires have no fuel
   C. Water always increases oxygen
   D. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Floating and Sinking 14 3.2. Sound Energy 14 3.3. Heat transfer 12 Total number ? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Floating and Sinking 14 3.2. Sound Energy 14 3.3. Heat transfer 12 Total number .
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Floating and Sinking 14 3.2. Sound Energy 14 3.3. Heat transfer 12 Total number .
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Floating and Sinking 14 3.2. Sound Energy 14 3.3. Heat transfer 12 Total number .
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Floating and Sinking 14 3.2. Sound Energy 14 3.3. Heat transfer 12 Total number .

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Mixtures 14 2.2. Water Pollution 18 3.0. Force and Energy 3.1. Floating and Sink? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Mixtures 14 2.2. Water Pollution 18 3.0. Force and Energy 3.1. Floating and Sink.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Mixtures 14 2.2. Water Pollution 18 3.0. Force and Energy 3.1. Floating and Sink.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Mixtures 14 2.2. Water Pollution 18 3.0. Force and Energy 3.1. Floating and Sink.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Mixtures 14 2.2. Water Pollution 18 3.0. Force and Energy 3.1. Floating and Sink.

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Sound Energy? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Sound Energy.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Sound Energy.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Sound Energy.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Sound Energy.

7. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Paper burning to ash
   B. Iron rusting
   C. Ice melting to water
   D. Milk souring

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Mixtures? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Mixtures.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Mixtures.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Mixtures.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Mixtures.

9. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 0 °C
   B. 50 °C
   C. 37 °C
   D. 100 °C

10. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. joule (J)
   B. newton (N)
   C. watt (W)
   D. pascal (Pa)

11. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only carbon dioxide
   B. Glucose and oxygen
   C. Nitrogen gas only
   D. Only water vapour

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Heat transfer? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Heat transfer.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Heat transfer.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Heat transfer.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Heat transfer.

13. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   B. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   C. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   D. A compound can be separated by filtering only

14. Which practice best shows correct science when studying The Human Breathing system 18 2.0. Matter 2.1. Mixtures 14 2.2. Water Pollution ? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about The Human Breathing system 18 2.0. Matter 2.1. Mixtures 14 2.2. Water Pollution .
   B. Guess results without recording observations on The Human Breathing system 18 2.0. Matter 2.1. Mixtures 14 2.2. Water Pollution .

   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to The Human Breathing system 18 2.0. Matter 2.1. Mixtures 14 2.2. Water Pollution .

15. Which practice best shows correct science when studying The Human Breathing System? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to The Human Breathing System.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about The Human Breathing System.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Human Breathing System.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on The Human Breathing System.

16. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Classification of Plants? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Classification of Plants.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Classification of Plants.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Classification of Plants.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Classification of Plants.
